title: Staging batch
description: The envelope an agent writes to data/staging/<batch>.json. Nothing here reaches the canonical store until a human moves it. The three array fields at the top level are all required on purpose: an agent that reports only what it kept cannot be reviewed.

batch.description: Batch identifier, conventionally <date>-<source>. Appears in the filename too.

unresolved.description: Names or references that could not be resolved to an existing entity. NEVER auto-create these — a human decides. Empty means you checked and found none, not that you skipped the check.

deliberately_discarded.description: What was seen and NOT kept, with a reason and a location. This is the only place a reviewer can catch content misfiled as noise; an empty list is a red flag rather than a clean result.

content.description: Short summary — not the original text.

location.description: Where in the source, so a reviewer can go and look.

routing_table.description: Required for extraction agents. Every input passage appears here with the categories it was split into. Reconcile in BOTH directions before delivering: every passage present, and every tag having a counterpart in the output.

type.description: Entity or relation type in your schema.

key.description: Stable identifier — the thing you resolve against, not the display name.

fields.description: Payload. Use null for a value the controlled vocabulary cannot express; do not substitute the nearest term.

source.description: Who said it: URL, document id + location, or informant.

retrieved_at.description: When it was collected. Not bookkeeping — once sources coexist, 'which is current' is unanswerable without it.

measurement_conditions.description: For measured values: under what conditions. Two sources that appear to contradict each other may have measured different things.

confidence.description: Low is a legitimate value. Use it when a field was inferred from prose rather than read as stated.
